reason: On all 91 factorial calibration questions a single terminal source offset in the registered discrete family cannot gain 0.02, even with access to true returns. Extending the very same case-transfer rule to the first write makes a larger gain feasible on these data. This amendment follows examination of those training outcomes. It does not supersede the original terminal-only protocol.
policy: Use the identical frozen Llama model, donor exclusion, three prompt treatments, order-balanced votes and bounded native-logit corrections at both writes. For the first decision show only the first session. For the second show only the current second session; condition its native propensity on the realized prior action. Share the frozen terminal votes for the same source across both prefixes. The two sources never see one another's votes, future source text or target benchmark QA.
population: Register all 12 calibration windows (91 questions) and all 52 randomized later windows (466 questions). Reuse the exact 37 previously registered terminal prompt packets, collect 64 root and 27 additional terminal packets. Interleave early and later windows in the original frozen order. Report exact four-path returns in calibration, focal and design-weighted joint F1 on randomized pairs, per-question rows, usage and fixed-visit comparisons. Match each node's observed mean propensity across eligible windows without using outcomes. Record any previously published path scores and mark a window numerically prospective only when BOTH packets predate its first score. State which previous terminal forecasts existed on registration.
gates: Use all 40 windows / 378 questions starting in session 13 or later as the primary later block. Require at least 90% coverage, gains over native in at least four dialogues, +0.02 focal F1 over native and full terminal PPO, positive focal difference over raw-return, semantic-only, permuted and matched-rate, and positive joint design-weighted F1 over native. Require at least one strictly prospective window in this block and a positive prospective focal difference over native. Then evaluate independent development; the original complete LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S tests remain required.
